newsitem.title: USA: China interest in U.S. soybeans likely - exporters.
newsitem.headline: China interest in U.S. soybeans likely - exporters.

text.p: Export traders on Tuesday said they could not confirm market rumors that China is seeking or has bought U.S. soybeans this week, but they said they expect such transactions to occur soon as harvest pressures prices.
A rumor that China was seeking 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans circulated at the Chicago Board of Trade Tuesday morning.
"I would not be surprised for China to seek this amount since we are looking at them to import 1.5 million tonnes soybeans," one senior U.S. exporter said.
Of that amount, China will likely import 500,000 tonnes from the United States and one million tonnes from South America, he said.
"It is always a big question mark when they will come in or won't come," the exporter said.
"Chinese buyers are in constant exploration for market values but we have no indication of any buying," he added.
China bought 422,800 tonnes of U.S. soybeans in the 1995/96 marketing year ended on August 31, 1996, against nil the prior year.

No sales to China for the current season have been reported but the exporter noted that 1.235 million tonnes of soybeans have been booked under "unknown destinations" in the U.S. Agriculture Department's weekly sales report, as of Sept 5.
"So there could be some Chinese sales in there and the destinations have not been declared yet," the exporter said.
A second exporter heard China was seeking at least 50,000 tonnes U.S. soybeans last weekend for October/November shipment.
"People were telling me 200,000 tonnes, but I had heard of 50,000 tonnes," he said. "If it was more, I do not know. I believe they got it but I cannot confirm that."

A third trader at a U.S. export firm said that, for the past few weeks, China has been actively buying Brazilian soymeal and possibly U.S. soymeal. For them to seek 200,000 tonnes of soybeans was not out of the question, he said.
"China has been in the oilseed and protein markets, so I guess I would not be surprised," the third exporter said.
Traders said the Chinese soybean crop had not come up to expectations and so they needed soybeans to crush.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture on September 12 estimated China's soybean production this year at 13.30 million tonnes, against 13.50 million a year earlier.
U.S. soybean production is expected to rise to 61.8 million tonnes, from 53.56 million last year, representing about 50 percent of world output.
